clue.text: Unqualified doctor bales out

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A struck-off doctor bails out of a failing practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like the unqualified person, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange BALES OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Unqualified support is total, with no reservations attached.

clue.text: Gold diggers' territory invested in state railroad

annotationWithheld.why: Gold diggers' territory invested in state railroad (8): BULLDOZE defined by 'railroad', but no reading of 'state' plus a gold-field territory (OZ?) inside it gives BULLDOZE; parse not found
annotationWithheld.clue: Gold diggers' territory invested in state railroad

clue.text: Rejected hot food we cooked when safe from danger

parts.note: something rejected is thrown out

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are worked up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone rejected a hot meal that had been prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns HOT FOOD WE into OFTHEWOOD; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being past the worst of a crisis, no longer in peril.

clue.text: A foreign sort of grub can be rough!

parts.note: un is French for 'a'
a gentle is an angler's name for a maggot used as bait

explanation.surface: A complaint that some foreign food can be coarse.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'gentle' is a maggot, used by anglers as bait.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough treatment is harsh and lacking any tenderness.

clue.text: Find marrow in a delicatessen? Certainly.

indicators.note: in tells you the letters run inside the words delicatessen and certainly

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether a deli stocks marrows, and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marrow' looks like the vegetable; it is the core or heart of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The marrow of a matter is its innermost core, its vital substance.

clue.text: A tower said to be of interest

indicators.note: said tells you the words are to be pronounced, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a peel is a small fortified tower, found on the Scottish border

explanation.surface: Someone claims a certain tower is interesting.
explanation.walkthrough: A peel (or pele) is a small defensive tower built in the Anglo-Scottish borders.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeal is attractiveness, the quality that draws interest.

clue.text: What to wear in the south of France?

definitions.text: What to wear in the south of France?

parts.words: What to wear in the south of France?
parts.note: the French name for the southern region of France doubles as a skirt length reaching mid-calf

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both southern France and a calf-length skirt or dress style.

clue.text: Bachelor always on time for a drink

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A bachelor who is always punctual turns up for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Any liquid taken for refreshment, such as tea or beer, is a drink.

clue.text: Perhaps I worked in stone

indicators.note: worked means shaped or fashioned, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sculptor modestly suggests they carved in stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked in stone' reads as sculpting; 'worked' rearranges PERHAPS I and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue gemstone, a variety of corundum.

clue.text: Monotonous bit of scenery

definitions.meaning: dull and lacking variety, like an unchanging tone
in the theatre, a painted canvas screen forming part of a stage set

explanation.surface: A theatre critic finds part of the set dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a dull, lifeless quality and a theatre's painted scenery panel.

clue.text: 20 in training, having recovered from worry

parts.note: once you have got past an illness you are said to be over it
to exercise someone is to trouble or vex them

explanation.surface: An athlete pushes too hard in training after getting past their anxieties.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 across is GO TOO FAR, so the definition is going too far in training.
explanation.definitionFit: Training too hard is overstepping the mark in physical work.

clue.text: Oppose intention of top man

parts.note: to counter is to oppose
the tenor of something is its general drift or intended meaning

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to oppose the boss's plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top man' looks like a chief; it is a male singer with the highest voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A male alto, singing in the highest male vocal range.

clue.text: Suicidal little singer in The Mikado

definitions.text: Suicidal little singer in The Mikado

parts.words: Suicidal little singer in The Mikado
parts.note: in Ko-Ko's song 'Tit-willow' a small bird dies of grief by flinging itself into a river

explanation.surface: A tragic minor performer in the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' suggests a cast member, but it is a songbird in a song from Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The small songbird of the opera's song, a tit, is the one that drowns itself.

clue.text: Port of call very nearly ignored by army

indicators.note: very nearly says the word call is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to cut someone is to ignore them pointedly
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A ship's port of call is almost snubbed by soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city, now Kolkata, is a major seaport on the Hooghly.

clue.text: Withdraws unconstitutional decrees

indicators.note: unconstitutional suggests something out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A government withdraws decrees found to be illegal.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to move back or retreat, as a tide does.

clue.text: Harshness shown by free city — not the first to capture a soldier

indicators.note: to capture means one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: to rid is to free
GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: not the first says the word city loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: A liberated city shows harshness by taking a soldier prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigidity is strictness or severity, unbending sternness.

clue.text: Highlight part of the face

definitions.meaning: a main attraction or prominent item

explanation.surface: Make-up advice: emphasise one area of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a special attraction and one facial element such as the nose.

clue.text: Altercation in the market

definitions.meaning: a place of trade, as in a stock or corn trading hall

explanation.surface: A row breaks out among traders.
explanation.definitionFit: An angry exchange of words, and a building where commodities or stocks are traded.

clue.text: Obstruction in the course of a game

indicators.note: in places one piece within another

parts.note: a route is a course taken
let means hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Something gets in the way during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let' as an obstruction survives in the legal phrase 'without let or hindrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino gambling game played with a spinning wheel and ball.

clue.text: Crawl clear from a systematic search

parts.note: to drag is to move slowly, to crawl
net means clear, as in profit after deductions

explanation.surface: Police crawl clear of a thorough hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A coordinated police sweep to catch suspects.

clue.text: Overstep the mark in unconventional love of argot

indicators.note: unconventional means irregular, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An unusual fondness for slang goes beyond acceptable bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for exceeding acceptable limits.

clue.text: Ploughs, embodying many other agricultural instruments

indicators.note: embodying means containing, so one piece holds another

parts.note: to plough is British slang for failing an exam
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number

explanation.surface: Ploughs and many other farm tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ploughs' looks like the farm tools; it is British student slang for failing an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand threshing tools, another farm implement besides ploughs.

clue.text: A noisy scene in the ring

definitions.text: A noisy scene in the ring

parts.words: A noisy scene in the ring
parts.note: reads as a boxing-ring brawl but describes a rowdy spectacle and a show staged in a big top ring

explanation.definitionFit: A word for a chaotic uproar and for a travelling show performed in a ring.

clue.text: Dull speech in Latin, for example

parts.note: dead means dull or lifeless
language is speech

explanation.surface: A tedious oration in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is a tongue no longer spoken natively.

clue.text: A drink for lords and ladies

parts.note: rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A tipple for aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lords and ladies' is the folk name of the wild cuckoo-pint plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lords and ladies is the common British name of a wild arum lily.

clue.text: Record of distinction

definitions.meaning: eminence, as in 'a person of some standing'

explanation.surface: A record of someone's eminence.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief written memo, and fame or standing.

clue.text: Admittedly depressed but extremely loyal

parts.note: true, as in 'true, it was late'
blue means sad

explanation.surface: Someone is down but staunchly faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: Staunchly faithful, especially to the Conservative party.

clue.text: Speculative views of ambassador accepted by politicians

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in by the politicians, one piece inside another

parts.note: Tories are British Conservative politicians
HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: An envoy's opinions are adopted by MPs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypotheses: ideas proposed to explain something.
